questions.question: Which polyatomic ionic compound is a white, crystalline powder used in fire extinguishers and to neutralise acids and bases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium Bicarbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium bicarbonate, commonly known as baking soda, is a white crystalline powder that is often used as a leavening agent in baking.
 
• It is widely used in fire extinguishers due to its ability to produce carbon dioxide when heated, which helps to suffocate fires.
 
• Sodium bicarbonate can neutralize acids and bases, making it a useful compound in various chemical reactions and for pH control.
 
• It is also used in medical applications, for instance, to treat acid indigestion and heartburn by neutralizing stomach acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sodium Bisulphite:**

 
 
• Sodium bisulphite (NaHSO3) is a chemical compound commonly used as a food preservative and in the treatment of wastewater.
 
• It has reducing properties and is used in various industrial applications to prevent oxidation.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Thiosulphate:**
 
 
• Sodium thiosulphate (Na2S2O3) is an inorganic compound used in photographic processing, gold extraction, and medical treatment of cyanide poisoning.
 
• It is also used in water treatment to dechlorinate water before disposal or reuse.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Chromate:**
 
 
• Sodium chromate (Na2CrO4) is a chemical compound used in the manufacture of pigments, coatings, and other industrial applications.
 
• It is highly toxic and carcinogenic, and its use is regulated due to environmental and health concerns.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate:**
 
 
• Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) is a versatile compound with applications in baking, cleaning, fire extinguishing, and medical treatments.
 
• It is a mild base that can neutralize acids and is used in various household and industrial applications.

questions.question: What is the adulterant of hot paprika?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sudan dye**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sudan dye** is a synthetic chemical used to color products and is considered an adulterant in hot paprika.
 
• It is not permitted in food products as it **poses health risks, including being potentially carcinogenic**.
 
• Detection of Sudan dye in food items is a significant concern for food safety authorities.
 
• Other common adulterants in spices may include starch powder, chalk powder, and sawdust, but Sudan dye is specifically noted for its use in hot paprika.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Food adulteration** refers to the process of adding or mixing something inferior, harmful, or unnecessary to food items, reducing their quality, safety, and nutritional value.
 
• Authorities like the **Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)** monitor and regulate food safety standards to prevent adulteration.
 
• Consumers are advised to purchase spices and food products from reputable sources and check for certifications indicating quality and safety standards.

questions.question: Why is hydrogen used as fuel in a cryogenic engine?

options.text: Because it is easy to store at room temperature.
Because it has the highest energy output per kilogram.
Because it is very cheap in comparison to other fuels.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Because it has the highest energy output per kilogram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Hydrogen** is widely used as a fuel in cryogenic engines because it has the **highest energy output per kilogram**. This makes it an extremely efficient fuel source, especially for applications like space exploration where energy density is crucial.
 
• With a **specific energy of approximately 142 MJ/kg**, hydrogen far exceeds the energy output of conventional fuels like gasoline or kerosene.
 
• In cryogenic engines, hydrogen is used in its liquid form (**liquid hydrogen or LH2**), which requires extremely low temperatures (**-253°C**) to remain in a liquid state. This enhances its energy density and usability in such applications.
 
• Other properties of hydrogen, such as its **low molecular weight** and ability to produce only water as a by-product when burned with oxygen, make it an environmentally friendly and efficient option for cryogenic engines.
 
• The use of hydrogen as a fuel is particularly significant in the **aerospace industry**, where it powers rockets like the Space Shuttle Main
